stated_mission: Mozilla Foundation's grantmaking program; MTF specifically funds open source technology projects with awards up to $50,000 plus a year of mentorship/support and access to Mozilla Fellows as subject-matter mentors.
funding_priorities: Open source technology projects (theme rotates per cycle)
Recent cycles per web search (not primary-source confirmed): AI transparency/bias, environmental justice + AI
A separate 'Democracy x AI Cohort 2026' also ran under Mozilla Foundation, initial proposals due 2026-03-16 (already closed)
grant_size_range: Up to $50,000 (MTF); note MOSS, the predecessor program, historically ranged $5,000-$150,000+ but MOSS itself is defunct
application_cycle: Thematic, rotating focus per call; no evidence of a currently open general call as of 2026-08-20
application_process: Historically an online call-for-proposals per themed cycle. As of 2026-08-20, the MTF-specific call-for-proposals URL redirects to Mozilla Foundation's generic Grantmaking landing page, which lists no active/open MTF call.
eligibility_requirements: Must have a working product or prototype in hand — idea-stage projects are not considered. Doikayt/geoCRM: prototype already exists (confirmed by Chris, 2026-08-20), so this specific bar is met.

Per web search only (not confirmed on Mozilla's own site, which redirected away): individuals, teams, nonprofits, and sometimes for-profits are eligible; unregistered/unincorporated organizations reportedly can apply via a legally registered fiscal host — requires direct confirmation once MTF's own eligibility page is reachable.

Recent call themes (AI transparency/bias; environmental justice + AI; Democracy x AI) do not obviously match Doikayt's GASify/geoCRM domain (GAS tooling / grassroots CRM) — fit depends entirely on whatever the next call's theme turns out to be.

mission_alignment.sponsor_mission_summary: Mozilla Foundation funds open-source technology projects advancing public-interest goals; MTF specifically funds prototype-stage projects, one grant cycle at a time, around a rotating theme (recent cycles: AI transparency/bias, then environmental justice + AI).
mission_alignment.doikayt_overlap: Doikayt is exactly the kind of small, open-source, prototype-stage, technologist-led project MTF's general model targets — but none of MTF's recently published themes (AI, environmental justice, democracy) map cleanly onto GASify/geoCRM's actual domain.
potential_concerns: No currently open call as of 2026-08-20
Thematic mismatch with recent cycles (AI-centric; GASify/geoCRM is not an AI project)
Fiscal-sponsor acceptance not yet primary-source confirmed
mission_alignment.best_fit_framing: If a future MTF call's theme is broad enough to include general open-source movement-tech infrastructure (not AI-specific), position GASify/geoCRM as grassroots-org-controlled infrastructure resisting Big Tech dependency — echoes Mozilla's own 'healthy internet' framing. Not a fit under the current/recent AI-specific themes.

status.current_assessment: MOSS (Mozilla's historical open-source grant program) is defunct — on indefinite hiatus since Mozilla's 2020 restructuring, not accepting applications. Its stated successor is the Mozilla Technology Fund (MTF), up to $50k per award with a year of mentorship. However: (1) MTF's own call-for-proposals URL currently redirects to Mozilla Foundation's generic Grantmaking landing page, which lists no active/open MTF call as of 2026-08-20 — MTF appears to run periodic themed cycles rather than being continuously open. (2) Recent cycle themes found via web search (not primary-source confirmed) were AI-transparency/bias, then environmental-justice+AI, plus a separate 'Democracy x AI Cohort 2026' that already closed 2026-03-16 — none obviously match GASify/geoCRM's domain. (3) MTF does require 'a product or working prototype in hand' (not idea-stage) — Chris confirmed geoCRM already has a working prototype, so that specific bar is met. (4) Fiscal-sponsor acceptance ('unregistered organisations... via a legally registered fiscal host') came from a search-engine synthesis, not Mozilla's own eligibility page directly, and needs primary-source confirmation before relying on it.
status.next_action: Watch for a future MTF call for proposals with a theme broad enough to plausibly include GASify/geoCRM (general open-source infrastructure, not AI-specific); re-verify eligibility (fiscal-sponsor acceptance, current grant size, deadline) directly against Mozilla's own site once a call is open, since current findings are largely search-derived rather than primary-source-confirmed.
